Article Title: A year after picking up the gun: The end of Kashmir’s last known active LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat

‘Lateef killed’

Kulgam: Security personnel gesture in celebration after gunning down top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Lateef Bhat during an encounter, in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: On November 18, 2025, Mohammad Lateef Bhat joined Lashkar-e-Taiba , according to police. Exactly a year later, he was killed in a gunfight in his home district of Kulgam. In between, the ‘A-category’ terrorist had become one of Kashmir ’s most wanted, with a Rs 15 lakh bounty on his head. Police said he had been tasked with disrupting peace and damaging the Valley’s economy.Categorised as an ‘A’ category operative, Bhat was one of the most wanted local terrorists in Kashmir. He had been linked to two attacks in July this year.Officials described Bhat as a former carpenter who finished his Class 12 in 2021 and then dropped out of college in the early days.In November 2025, he went missing and joined LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF), officials said.On July 22, he allegedly shot dead Jammu and Kashmir Police head constable Ashiq Hussain in a crowded market area at Lal Chowk in Anantnag. On July 31, he was reportedly involved in the murder of two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kulgam.Law enforcement agencies subsequently identified him from CCTV screen grabs of the Lal Chowk area that captured the cop’s murder. In August, the Jammu and Kashmir Police announced a reward of Rs 15 lakh for information leading to him and put up his posters across prominent places in Kashmir.The banner appealed to people to provide credible information about the terrorists’ movements or whereabouts.It assured them that the identity of informants would remain confidential and that a reward would be given for reliable information.The search continued over the following months. On November 8, a banner seeking information about four wanted terrorists surfaced at Pratap Park in Srinagar’s Lal Chowk area. Bhat was named on it, along with Bilal Ahmad Mir, Mohammad Umar Mir and Abid Qayoom Lone, all from Baramulla district. Bhat was believed to be active in the Kashmir Valley, while the other three were suspected of operating from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, officials said."After joining the banned organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba, he was receiving directions from across (the border) to disrupt peace here, hit tourism, and damage the economy,” Kulgam senior superintendent of Police Anayat Ali Choudhary said.You have all seen his three or four attacks and how ruthlessly he carried them out," he added, as per ANI.On November 11, Bhat and his associate Umar Nisar Dar opened fire on a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) checkpoint in the Akhran area near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, injuring three personnel. The attack took place at around 2.15 pm when two terrorists approached the checkpoint, which was manned by personnel of the CRPF's 46th Battalion.According to investigators, the attackers approached from a cluster of trees and dense vegetation. One of them opened indiscriminate fire with an AK-series rifle, while the other remained positioned on the road, providing cover. The CRPF personnel retaliated, forcing the attackers to flee through the surrounding vegetation.Investigators subsequently identified the attackers through CCTV footage that captured their movements during reconnaissance of potential targets in Mir Bazar, Akhran, Hablish and Killam on November 10, a day before the attack.The hunt that followed reached a turning point on Monday, when a gunfight broke out in the Larnoo area, around 100km south of Srinagar. Drones were deployed to scan the vast apple orchards and adjoining forests as security forces continued combing the area.Dar, was killed in that encounter. Bhat was also injured but managed to escape. He took shelter in a mosque located around 2-3 km away, having slipped away from the site of the earlier encounter near the Laru bypass.Police also suspected that Dar had been providing shelter and logistical assistance to Bhat for several months.Early Wednesday, security forces received specific intelligence inputs about Bhat’s location. The Jammu and Kashmir Police, CRPF and Army jointly launched a cordon-and-search operation around a mosque in Kulgam’s Zangalpora village after re-establishing contact with him.SSP Choudhary said the operation was carried out with careful planning and coordination among the security forces. Personnel made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including through a video call in which Choudhary personally spoke to him for an extended period.“We tried hard to persuade him to surrender, telling him that he is still young and has his whole life ahead of him. He did not agree and entered a mosque and opened fire around 2.45am,” Choudhary said.Security forces also made repeated announcements asking Bhat to surrender after he took shelter inside the mosque. He then opened fire on security personnel, triggering a gunfight.Because the mosque was within the cordoned-off area and Bhat was firing from inside it, Choudhary said, forces exercised maximum restraint. He added that personnel were strictly following standard operating procedures (SOPs) and would take as much time as necessary to neutralise him while minimising damage tothe religious structure.Security forces were seen celebrating after Bhat was neutralised, with personnel cheering “Lateef killed” as they returned after the operation.According to CRPF, Bhat’s killing after sustained operations in Kulgam sent a message that terrorists would not be allowed to escape after carrying out attacks, including those targeting security personnel."Congratulations guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather," DG CRPF GP Singh said in his X post.Home minister Amit Shah also celebrated the fall of “Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley”, congratulating the forces for executing the operation with a very high level of synergy.
Article Summary: Mohammad Lateef Bhat joined Lashkar-e-Taiba on November 18, 2025. Exactly a year later, he was killed in a gunfight in his home district of Kulgam. The ‘A-category’ terrorist had become one of Kashmir ’s most wanted, with a Rs 15 lakh bounty on his head.

Article Title: Air India crash: Centre says investigation at 'fag end'; report still awaited
Article Text:
Air India crash probe in final stages, Centre tells Supreme Court

What the preliminary report found

NEW DELHI: The investigation into the June 2025 Air India crash that killed 260 people is in its final stages, the Centre told the Supreme Court on Wednesday. It also sought more time to respond to a petition demanding an independent probe into the accident.“We are at the fag end of the investigation,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a bench led by the Chief Justice of India. He urged the court to adjourn the matter by two to three weeks, saying investigators had to follow international protocols.“There is no reason why we should delay deliberately,” Mehta said.The court agreed to take up the matter after two weeks. The hearing was on a petition filed by Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, father of the flight's captain Sumeet Sabharwal, seeking a separate and independent investigation into the crash.Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing in the matter, pointed out that the final investigation report had not yet been made public and sought an early hearing.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) had earlier informed the Supreme Court that it expected its final report into the crash by the first week of October 2026. That deadline has passed without the report being released.The Boeing 787 Dreamliner crashed shortly after taking off from Ahmedabad for London on June 12, 2025.Of the 242 people on board, 241 were killed, along with 19 people on the ground, taking the death toll to 260.A preliminary investigation report released in July 2025 found that the aircraft's engine fuel-control switches had moved from the “run” position to “cutoff” seconds after take-off, cutting off fuel supply to both engines. However, it did not establish why the switches had moved.The report also recorded a cockpit conversation in which one pilot was heard asking the other why the fuel supply had been cut off. The other pilot denied doing so. Investigators did not identify which pilot made either remark.Captain Sumeet Sabharwal's father has questioned the investigation, alleging that AAIB officials had implied during a visit to his home that his son was responsible for cutting off the fuel supply to the engines.In July, the AAIB told the Supreme Court that it had prepared a transcript of the cockpit voice recorder and conducted a psychological autopsy as part of its investigation. It had said a draft final report would be prepared around October and circulated to participating countries for comments before being finalised and published.The final report is expected to provide further findings on the circumstances surrounding the crash.
Article Summary: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner crashed shortly after taking off from Ahmedabad for London on June 12, 2025. Of the 242 people on board, 241 were killed, along with 19 people on the ground, taking the death toll to 260. A preliminary investigation report released in July 2025 found that the aircraft's engine fuel-control switches had moved.

Article Title: 'Should be publicly flogged': Sena vs Sena escalates after Shaina NC 'tears' Balasaheb's photo

NEW DELHI: A war of words erupted between the rival Shiv Sena factions on Wednesday after Sena (UBT) leaders accused Shinde Sena leader Shaina NC of disrespecting Bal Thackeray by tearing his photograph.While Sena (UBT) leaders demanded a "public flogging" of those who insulted Balasaheb, Shaina hit back, claiming that she had actually torn a photograph of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar The controversy erupted during a protest by the Shinde-led faction against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's recently released memoir. Party workers tore pages from the book on camera, during which Shaina allegedly tore a photograph of Bal Thackeray.Shiv Sena (UBT) seized on the incident to question the rival faction's claim to Bal Thackeray's legacy.In a post on social media, Sena (UBT) leader Swati Borkar said, "Shame on you Shaina NC. You have once again proved that none of you can ever be true Shiv Sainiks of Balasaheb."Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut also criticised and accused the rival faction of "neither any ideology nor any morals.""Amit Shah’s Shinde Sena people are tearing up a photo of Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray. Because all these people are mercenaries, it’s a good thing these black-faced people with white feet have run away!" Raut said."These people have neither any ideology nor any morals, neither a single leader nor any loyalty. All these people who insult the honorable Balasaheb should be publicly flogged! I hope at least the Marathi people won’t object to my language!" he added.Shaina, however, denied the accusation claiming that the picture was of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar. She accused Sena (UBT) of twisting the incident to create a false narrative."Show me where I have torn or disrespected Hindu 'hruday samrat' Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated. Anyone spreading defamatory claims against me will face legal action," she wrote on X."And yes, as I have said, I will tear Mani Shankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us," she added.Earlier in the day, Shinde-led Sena workers tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's book during a protest in Mumbai, demanding that publisher HarperCollins remove passages on pages 201 and 443.Addressing a press conference, Shaina accused Gandhi of insulting Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar by describing him as a "Hindutva exclusionary"."Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. She calls him a Hindutva exclusionary. But Balasaheb Thackeray always said that Savarkar is the soul of Hindutva," she said.Shaina also questioned Gandhi's delay in obtaining Indian citizenship, contrasting it with Savarkar's contribution to the freedom struggle."Sonia ji, it took you 15-plus years to even initiate the process of Indian citizenship. Savarkar gave 50-plus years of his life, not just in jail, but also for the cause of Bharat. Who are you to judge?" she said.Accusing Sonia Gandhi of attempting to rewrite history, Shaina said Maharashtra would not forgive her."We demand that HarperCollins eliminate pages 201 and 443. Savarkar spent 11 years in Kala Pani for India's freedom. Balasaheb Thackeray worshipped Savarkar," she said.She also questioned Gandhi's understanding of the RSS and its role in nation-building, as well as the sacrifices made during India's freedom struggle.
Article Summary: Shinde Sena leader Shaina NC accused of disrespecting Bal Thackeray by tearing his photograph. Sena (UBT) leaders demanded a "public flogging" of those who insulted Balasaheb. Shaina hit back, claiming that she had actually torn a photograph of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar.

Article Title: 9 in 10 Indian firms hit by AI agents in past year; only a third contained it within a day: Survey
Article Text:

A report released on Wednesday has found that 92 per cent of Indian organisations surveyed experienced a security incident linked to AI agents in the last 12 months. Only 36 per cent, however, were able to contain such an incident within 24 hours, PTI reported.The survey by ServiceNow, which covered 500 security leaders, showed that although half of Indian respondents rated their agentic security capabilities as established, many organisations still lacked basic governance and monitoring mechanisms, PTI reported.The report, titled Deployed but Ungoverned: The State of Agentic Security in India, said just 19 per cent of organisations had one named person accountable for governing agentic AI security. Only 18 per cent had unified visibility of their AI agents through a single interface.The study also pointed to shortcomings in pre-deployment security checks. Just 30 per cent of organisations had an automated deployment gate that stopped AI agents from going live until they cleared security checks, while 47 per cent could provide a complete evidence package on demand.“India’s AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to understand, monitor and govern the agentsenterprises deploy. Knowing what an agent can reach is not the same as seeing what it is doing.Automated controls and continuous oversight will be essential to keeping AI innovation underpinned by trust and cyber resilience,” Kulmeet Bawa, GVP and managing director for India and SAARC at ServiceNow, said, according to PTI.Bawa noted that AI agents were now a part of how Indian enterprises function, but security had failed to keep pace. He emphasised that every agent should be registered, given an owner and made visible in a single place, with automated controls and swift responses to help security teams spot and contain issues.The report further found that 51 per cent of organisations had automated, real-time detection of unusual AI agent behaviour, yet 67 per cent were unable to respond automatically when an agent behaved anomalously.In addition, 37 per cent of organisations had found AI agents running in production over the past 12 months that were never registered or known to their security teams.
Article Summary: 92 per cent of Indian organisations surveyed experienced a security incident linked to AI agents in the last 12 months. Only 36 per cent, however, were able to contain such an incident within 24 hours. Only 18 per cent had unified visibility of their AI agents through a single interface.

Article Title: 'Purity of voter list': Yogi Adityanath defends SIR after 'missing' Hindu voters claim
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath has staunchly defended the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, emphasizing its role in maintaining the integrity of voter lists.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls amid a political row over his claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the state's electoral rolls. The CM backed the SIR process and asserted that the exercise was necessary to ensure the "purity" of voter lists.At News18 Rising Bharat Summit, Yogi Adityanath said the names of deceased persons and non-citizens should be removed from electoral rolls, while every eligible adult Indian citizen must be included. He also said the BJP workers would ensure that no eligible voter was left out and expressed confidence that the exercise would be conducted transparently."The names of voters who have passed away should be removed from the electoral rolls. The names of people who are not citizens of India should not be included in the electoral rolls. Every adult Indian citizen should have their name included in the voter list," he said.His remarks come a day after Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa clarified that the Election Commission's database does not maintain information on voters' religion or caste.Rinwa said the poll body could not officially classify missing voters on religious lines and ruled out any conspiracy to target a particular community.Earlier, Yogi Adityanath had claimed that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the electoral rolls after the SIR. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav had questioned the source of the chief minister's figures.Targeting the Congress over its allegations of vote theft and questions about the SIR and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), Yogi Adityanath said the party blamed constitutional institutions for its electoral failures."When they win, it is their victory, but when they lose, the EVM is wrong, the SIR is wrong, and the Election Commission is responsible," he said, accusing the Congress of undermining constitutional institutions.Taking a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, he alleged that the Congress leader became part of every campaign that was against India's interests or questioned its constitutional institutions."Unfortunately, there is still a lack of maturity. He should avoid such frivolous issues and speak on merit, facts and evidence," the CM said.Responding to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's remarks about adding another 'P' for 'Pandits' to his broader social coalition of "PDA", amid perceptions of discontent among Brahmins, Adityanath cited statements by some SP leaders and said their remarks and the party's past conduct towards Hindu communities reflected its actual position.Speaking at the News18 event, Yogi Adityanath also expressed confidence in the BJP's return to power in the 2027 assembly elections.Asked whether the BJP-led NDA would cross its target of 320 seats in the 403-member assembly, the chief minister said the party would receive public support, but stopped short of giving a direct numerical assurance."Ask any woman, youth, trader or poor person, and they will say the government should return to power. Those who dislike development, see negativity in every initiative and want an atmosphere of disorder will be disappointed," he said.Later, reacting to Yogi Adityanath's confidence that the BJP would win more than 320 seats, Congress leader Pawan Khera said: "Will they get 320 seats? Isn't this 100 seats short? But who will be the CM? He (Adityanath) alleges that Hindu votes have been cut. If they are still getting 320 seats, it means there has been some agreement and they know what will happen," Khera said.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath says names of deceased persons and non-citizens should be removed from electoral rolls. Uttar Pradesh chief minister says every eligible adult Indian citizen must be included. He also expressed confidence in the BJP's return to power in the 2027 assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notices to Congress, Cockroach Janta Party, AAP and AISA after taking note of an amended plea by traders' bodies alleging that their businesses were affected by protests held in Delhi.During the hearing, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that competing fundamental rights - the right to protest and the right to conduct business - must be balanced.Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, representing the traders' bodies, submitted that protests at Jantar Mantar disrupted businesses in Central Delhi, Live Law reported.He also raised objections to the designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue."I am also saying that Ramlila Ground is in the heart of the city. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday called the newly formed alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Aazad the "B team" of the Samajwadi Party and Congress.He alleged that the opposition parties had brought the two leaders together to damage the BJP ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.According to news agency PTI, speaking at the News18 Rising Bharat Summit: North Edition in Lucknow, Adityanath said the Samajwadi Party was attempting to pursue two political strategies simultaneously by bringing Owaisi and Chandrashekhar together."The Samajwadi Party has now started riding two boats, and we know that riding two boats ultimately leads to sinking. Keeping this possibility in mind, it has brought together the Hyderabad 'maulana' and Chandrashekhar so that they can create an atmosphere here," he said.This was Adityanath's first public reaction to the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, launched by Owaisi and Chandrashekhar in Lucknow on November 12. The two leaders have announced plans to jointly contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, aiming to prevent the BJP from returning to power for a third consecutive term.The alliance has positioned itself as a political platform for marginalised communities, including Dalits, minorities and backward sections, and has invited the Samajwadi Party, Congress and other opposition parties to join its effort to defeat the BJP.Targeting the Samajwadi Party over its appeal among Dalit voters, Adityanath alleged that the party had disrespected the community and its prominent personalities."Dalits do not want to look towards the Samajwadi Party because of the disrespect it has shown towards them and their great personalities. This is an attempt to damage the BJP and other parties," he said.Taking a swipe at Owaisi, Adityanath said, "I assure the Hyderabad maulana that when he leaves from here, he will remember that when a government is formed in Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad will become Bhagya Lakshmi Puram."Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav had welcomed the formation of the new front, saying it could cost the BJP two to three per cent of votes. However, he maintained that his party's alliance with the Congress under the INDIA bloc would continue.The alliance brings together two leaders seeking to expand their political influence among Muslim and Dalit voters in Uttar Pradesh.While Owaisi heads the AIMIM, Chandrashekhar leads the Azad Samaj Party and has built his political identity around Dalit rights and representation.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath called the newly formed alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Aazad the "B team" of the Samajwadi Party and Congress. The two leaders have announced plans to jointly contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat, the only surviving local terrorist in the Valley, was trapped in an ongoing encounter in Kulgam district. Despite being cornered, the most wanted terrorist refused to surrender despite an offer from security forces, news agency PTI reported, quoting officials on Wednesday.The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced the morning prayers.Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was urged to surrender. Videos of security forces appealing to him to lay down his arms surfaced on social media.Also Read| 'Some dishes best served cold': Top LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam encounter However, LeT commander Bhat refused to surrender.Security forces are exercising maximum restraint in the ongoing encounter with Lashkar commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, as the trapped terrorist is firing from inside a mosque located within the cordoned-off area, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Kulgam said.The encounter was launched following credible intelligence inputs from Jammu and Kashmir Police and was carried out with proper planning and coordination among security forces, the SSP said.Security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including speaking to him over a video call for an extended period. The SSP said they appealed to him to lay down his arms, reminding him that he was young and could still surrender, but he refused."He chose to take shelter inside a mosque. We made repeated announcements, urging him to surrender, but he did not relent. At around 3.45, he opened fire on security forces, triggering a gunfight," the SSP Anayat Ali Choudhary said.He stressed that security forces were exercising utmost restraint as the mosque was located in the middle of the cordoned-off area and the terrorist was firing from inside the religious structure."I would like to emphasise that we are setting an example by exercising maximum restraint, particularly because the mosque is located in the middle of the cordoned-off area. The terrorist is firing from inside the mosque. I want to assure you that we have maintained the utmost restraint and are strictly following the standard operating procedures (SOPs). We will neutralise the terrorist, but we will take the time necessary to do so. Time is on our side," he said.The SSP added that security forces were trying to ensure minimal damage to the mosque while working to neutralise the terrorist as soon as possible."For now, we are having maximum restraint. We will ensure that the mosque is minimally damaged. We will try to eliminate the terrorist as soon as possible," he said.The encounter comes two days after Umar Nisar Dar, one of the terrorists involved in the November 11 attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam, was killed in a gunfight near Laru bypass on Monday. Bhat had escaped from the encounter site.Both Bhat and Dar are suspected of carrying out the attack on the CRPF post, which left three paramilitary personnel injured.Earlier, Kashmir Zone Police announced the encounter on X, saying, "Encounter started with terrorists and joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam."After Dar was killed on Monday, security forces continued extensive searches across the area to track down Bhat. Contact with him was re-established during searches early Wednesday, triggering a fresh exchange of gunfire.Officials said Dar had allegedly sheltered Bhat and provided logistical support to him for nearly six months. The duo is also suspected of conducting reconnaissance before carrying out the attack on the CRPF post last week.Dar, a former breadmaker who had been reported missing by his family, was killed in the encounter on Monday, a week after joining The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based LeT.
Article Summary: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat was trapped in an ongoing encounter in Kulgam district. Despite being cornered, the most wanted terrorist refused to surrender despite an offer from security forces. The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced the morning prayers.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines, offering gifts that showcased the country's diverse regional craftsmanship, textile traditions and cultural heritage.The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. PM Modi also presented a Dokra artwork boat to Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Bidriware silver inlay vases to Myanmar and Brunei, a royal blue Banarasi silk stole to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and a Jaipur blue pottery artefact to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.The presents drew on traditional art forms and crafts from different parts of India, including Rajasthan, Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and the Deccan region.PM Modi gifted Trump a Golden Pichwaai painting from Nathdwara in Rajasthan. The traditional cloth-painting art is known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions.Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, Pichwaai paintings feature motifs such as lotuses, cows and trees, along with ornamental borders. Their golden finish gives the artwork a distinctive regal appearance.The Philippine President received a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet, a hand-knotted craft admired for its sheen, soft texture, intricate designs and durability.Made from fine silk, the carpets involve thousands of knots tied by skilled artisans. Some take months or even years to complete. Their designs often draw inspiration from Kashmir's natural beauty, featuring floral patterns, chinar leaves and geometric motifs.PM Modi presented a traditional Chola bronze sculpture to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The art form flourished between the ninth and thirteenth centuries under the Chola dynasty in South India.The sculptures are made using the traditional lost-wax casting technique, known as Madhuchista Vidhana. Each piece is individually handcrafted, making it unique.Known for their anatomical precision, graceful forms and expressive details, Chola bronzes also offer insights into the clothing, jewellery, hairstyles and artistic traditions of the period. They represent Tamil Nadu's metallurgical skills and artistic heritage.PM Modi gifted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim a traditional silver worked urli, a decorative Indian vessel adorned with intricate silver embellishments that showcase the skill of the country's metalworkers.Traditionally filled with water and decorated with floating flowers, the urli symbolises purity, prosperity, hospitality and harmony.Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet received a traditional Dokra artwork boat. The metal craft is made using the lost-wax casting technique, a tradition dating back more than 4,000 years.The handcrafted piece depicts a boat carrying figures and birds, reflecting community life and harmony with nature. Each artwork is individually modelled in wax before being cast in metal.The boat symbolises unity, cooperation, resilience and collective progress. The craft also preserves traditional skills and supports artisan livelihoods.PM Modi gifted Bidriware silver inlay vases from Bidar, Karnataka, to Myanmar and Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei.Bidriware is a traditional metal craft made from a zinc-and-copper alloy and decorated with intricate pure silver inlay. Artisans engrave patterns, insert silver wire and treat the surface to create its characteristic deep black finish, which contrasts with the silver designs.The floral and geometric motifs draw inspiration from the architectural heritage of Bidar Fort. The craft has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and represents the artistic traditions of the Deccan region.Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in a Sadheli box.Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole showcases the centuries-old textile traditions of Banaras. Its intricate motifs reflect the craftsmanship and precision of generations of weavers.The royal blue colour symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony, while the presentation in a Sadheli box represents India's warmth and cultural esteem.PM Modi gifted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese a traditional Jaipur blue pottery artefact from Rajasthan.The craft is known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs. Its pieces feature hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.PM Modi gifted Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone a rose quartz elephant with gold work, a decorative craft associated with Rajasthan's stone-carving centres, particularly Jaipur.The artwork is carved from natural rose quartz and polished to bring out its soft, translucent sheen. It is then decorated with intricate hand-painted gold detailing, floral motifs and traditional ornamental designs.Combining gemstone carving with miniature painting, the elephant symbolises strength, wisdom, dignity and royal grandeur in Indian tradition. Its gilded detailing reflects India's heritage of luxury handicrafts and royal decorative arts.Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received a traditional Rogan art painting from Kutch, Gujarat. Practised by a handful of artisan families in Nirona village, Rogan art is a rare, centuries-old textile painting tradition.The technique uses a thick, elastic paint prepared by boiling castor oil and mixing it with natural pigments. Artisans create intricate designs freehand on fabric using a slender metal stylus. The cloth is then folded to transfer a symmetrical mirror image onto the other half.Traditionally used in bridal trousseaus and festive attire, Rogan art is known for its intricate patterns, geometric precision and craftsmanship. It represents Kutch's cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans.PM Modi gifted Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmão a handcrafted agate bowl from Khambhat, Gujarat. Made from agate, a semi-precious gemstone, each bowl has distinctive natural bands, colours and textures, making every piece unique.Khambhat has been a centre of agate processing and stone carving for centuries. Skilled artisans carefully cut, shape and polish the stone to create decorative and functional objects.Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung received a traditional Indian leather wall hanging, a handcrafted decorative artwork rooted in the country's folk-art heritage.Artisans soften and stretch treated leather before creating intricate designs through perforation, embossing and painting. The artworks feature floral, geometric and wildlife motifs, often made using natural vegetable dyes.Rooted in rural traditions and passed down through generations, the craft reflects regional artistic styles and storytelling. It also helps preserve traditional skills and support artisan livelihoods.The gifts were presented during PM Modi's November 16-17 visit to the Philippines, where he attended the 23rd Asean-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit. He also participated in a Quad leaders' meeting with Trump, Takaichi and Albanese.During the visit, India and Asean adopted a joint statement on cooperation in disaster management. The two sides also agreed to strengthen early warning systems, share satellite data, conduct joint simulation exercises and promote the use of artificial intelligence in disaster risk assessment and response coordination.PM Modi announced several initiatives to deepen India's engagement with the region, including a maritime cooperation plan, a joint cyber forensics training programme, technical exchanges on nuclear energy, a space hackathon and cooperation on critical minerals.Other announcements included youth and start-up initiatives, enhanced scholarships for Asean students at Nalanda University and free e-visas for tourists from Asean countries.
Article Summary: PM Modi presented traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines. The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said India was heading towards an economic crisis, citing massive unemployment and deep-rooted concerns over the country's education system. He made the remarks during an event at Columbia University in New York as part of his US visit.Rahul's comments drew a strong response from the ruling BJP, with the party calling him a "leader of anti-India propaganda.""The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system,"Lok Sabha leader of opposition said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The former Congress president was responding to a question from moderator about India's youth. He said a section of young people expressing frustration with the current state of affairs came from middle-class families and had received formal education, but were increasingly disillusioned with their prospects."We've been studying this, we've been looking into this, and the reason is very interesting, which is that the crux of it is they do not see a future for themselves," he said.Rahul said that there was a growing disconnect between young people and their parents over career opportunities, saying the younger generation was questioning the advice and experiences of the previous generation."So what they're actually saying to their parents, and we're hearing this from the parents, listen, You're not successful, you don't have a job, you can't tell us to do what you did because it doesn't work," he said.He said unemployment, limited future opportunities and concerns about the education system were pressing challenges that could not be brushed aside.BJP hit back at Rahul over his remarks in the US, accusing the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad.Leading the charge, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari took to X and called Rahul a "leader of anti-India propaganda"."Rahul Gandhi insults India at Columbia University! Article Title: Ankita Bhandari case: Parents demand Vinod Arya's narco test, call details from night of murder

Ankita's parents demand probe into Vinod Arya

NEW DELHI: Ankita Bhandari's parents have demanded a narco test of former BJP leader Vinod Arya, father of the main accused Pulkit Arya in the 2022 murder case , and sought an examination of his call detail records (CDRs) from the night of the incident. They warned of protests across Uttarakhand until their demands are met.Speaking to the media on Tuesday, Ankita's father, Virendra Singh Bhandari, said Vinod Arya should also be investigated, alleging that he had repeatedly travelled between Delhi and Uttarakhand around the time of the murder. He urged the CBI to examine the matter, conduct Vinod Arya's narco test and retrieve his call details."I want that now we will not spare Vinod Arya either, and the CBI investigation into the policeman is going on, Vinod Arya's narco test will be done, and his call details will be extracted, because when the incident with my girl happened, even on that day I told the government and the police to arrest Vinod Arya first and send him to jail, because he was repeatedly going to Delhi and coming back from there," Virendra Singh Bhandari said.He further alleged that discussions involving senior political leaders were taking place in Delhi at the time and questioned the alleged VIP angle in the case.Referring to the appointment of former BJP Uttarakhand incharge Dushyant Kumar Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim, Virendra said the family had opposed the move and submitted a memorandum at India Gate in Delhi."The same thing happened that that VIP has been made the Governor of Sikkim today, and during that time too, as soon as I heard on October 12 that he has been made the Governor of Sikkim, immediately on October 14 we sat at India Gate and submitted a memorandum to His Excellency the National Council that until the investigation is fulfilled, Sikkim's Governor Dushyant Kumar Gautam should not be appointed, and despite that, on October 19 he was made the Governor of Sikkim," he said.Virendra also referred to recent remarks made by Vinod Arya about his daughter and reiterated the family's demand for a thorough probe, including a narco test and retrieval of call records. He warned that protests would continue across Uttarakhand until the demands were fulfilled."And the day before yesterday, just like Vinod Arya spoke nonsense about my girl, in the same way we want that now the CBI investigation that is going on should be done, Vinod Arya's narco test should be done, and his call details should be extracted, and across Uttarakhand, until his CBI investigation, his narco test and his call details are not extracted, we will protest across Uttarakhand," Virendra Bhandari said.The fresh demands come amid an escalating row over the alleged VIP angle in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case. On November 15, Vinod Arya demanded an investigation into Ankita's parents, alleging they had "harassed, humiliated, and coerced" her before the incident.Addressing a press conference in Haridwar, Arya cited a compilation of alleged chat logs running into around 4,800 pages and claimed his son was not mentioned in the conversations. He also appealed to Uttarakhand chief minister to take action against those who allegedly drove the 19-year-old to distress.Reiterating that there was no political angle or VIP involvement in the case, Arya said, "The chat consists of approximately 4,800 pages... to our knowledge, there is no VIP involved in this entire case. We have no connection to the elections, nor are we trying to steer the narrative. Our sole demand is that action be taken against those who harassed Ankita, which is her father and mother."Questioning the charges against resort staff, Arya claimed low-wage employees were unfairly implicated due to public pressure, which he alleged had led to severe tragedies in their families.Meanwhile, additional director general of police (Crime and Law & Order), Uttarakhand, V Murugesan, said police acted promptly in the case and arrested all three accused within 24 hours of the incident.Ankita's parents had earlier staged a sit-in at India Gate in Delhi opposing Dushyant Kumar Gautam's appointment as Sikkim Governor until the CBI probe was concluded. They were detained by police and later released from Tilak Marg Police Station.The case pertains to the September 2022 murder of 19-year-old Ankita, a receptionist at a resort near Rishikesh. Her family has opposed the appointment of anyone whose name surfaced during the investigation to a constitutional post without being cleared by investigative agencies.
Article Summary: Ankita Bhandari's parents demand a narco test of former BJP leader Vinod Arya. They also seek an examination of his call detail records (CDRs) from the night of the incident. They warned of protests across Uttarakhand until their demands are met.

Article Title: Plea alleges Sonia Gandhi used forged papers for 1980 voter entry; court seeks police report

Court seeks Delhi Police report on plea alleging Sonia Gandhi's name in voter list before citizenship

How the case reached the ACJM court

NEW DELHI: Rouse Avenue Court on Wednesday sought an Action Taken Report (ATR) from the station house officer (SHO) of Delhi's IP Estate Police Station on complaint alleging that senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi 's name was included in the electoral rolls before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.Additional chief judicial magistrate (ACJM) Vinod Joshi issued the direction on a complaint filed by advocate Vikas Tripathi on August 24, 2025. The court has scheduled the next hearing for November 28.During Wednesday's proceedings, the complainant submitted attested copies of the electoral rolls for 1980, 1981 and 1983. However, the court directed him to place the original attested copies of the voter lists on record.Senior advocate Ajay Burman appeared on behalf of Tripathi.The complaint alleges that Sonia Gandhi's name featured in the electoral roll in 1980, nearly three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983. It raises questions over the alleged inclusion of her name in the voter lists during a period when she was not an Indian citizen.The court had earlier, on November 11, allowed the complainant to submit additional documents in support of his allegations.The proceedings follow a remand by the Session Court, which sent the matter back to the ACJM court for fresh consideration.The Session Court had set aside a 2025 order by the magistrate refusing to direct the registration of an FIR against Sonia Gandhi.On September 21, Special Judge (MP-MLA cases) Vishal Gogne allowed a revision petition filed by Tripathi challenging the Magistrate's order.While setting aside the earlier order, the Sessions Court observed that the complaint had been rejected on the basis of photocopies of unverified records."The order is an non speaking order. It is liable to be set aside," Special Judge Gogne had observed.The revisional court also questioned the magistrate's observations on the jurisdiction of the Central Government and the Election Commission in matters relating to citizenship.It held that the findings concerning the roles of these authorities in the citizenship issue were improper. The Sessions Court further noted that the earlier order did not adequately explain whether the complaint disclosed the commission of a cognisable offence.Referring to the allegations and documents submitted by the complainant, the Sessions Court noted that Sonia Gandhi's name was allegedly included in the electoral roll in 1980, removed in 1982 and added again in 1983.The court also pointed out that electoral rolls are meant for Indian citizens and referred to documents submitted by the complainant that allegedly listed Sonia Gandhi's name alongside her residential address at Safdarjung Road in New Delhi.However, the Sessions Court clarified that it could not assume the role of the Magistrate and decide the complaint itself. It remanded the matter for fresh consideration, directing the magistrate to seek a status report from the concerned police officer and pass a reasoned order after hearing the officer.The matter is now before the ACJM court in accordance with the Sessions Court's directions. The allegations against Sonia Gandhi remain part of the complaint and are yet to be adjudicated.
Article Summary: Court seeks Delhi Police report on plea alleging Sonia Gandhi's name in voter list before citizenship. Court seeks an Action Taken Report (ATR) from the station house officer (SHO) of Delhi's IP Estate Police Station. Complaint alleges that senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral rolls before she acquired Indian citizenship in April 1983.

US president Donald Trump arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where he was received by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the airport.He is also scheduled to hold a trilateral meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.Trump has said he intends to discuss limiting nuclear weapons and ending the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 following Russia's invasion. However, his aides had earlier told reporters that the Ukraine conflict would not feature in the trilateral meeting.The US president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opportunity to resolve the conflict, expressing optimism about the prospects of an agreement.“I think it’s very close to getting it done,” Trump said. “We’re going to have a good meeting on that.”Trump also raised the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, although neither engagement has been confirmed.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was “serious” about meeting Kim to address tensions with North Korea. However, he indicated that no meeting between the two leaders had been scheduled for Thursday.“I’m not telling you that there will be a meeting tomorrow,” Rubio said. “I’m just saying that" the president "is willing to meet and discuss, as he did during his first term.”Trump's visit to China follows his participation in the Asean summit and the Quad leaders' meeting in Manila. The Russian-Chinese foreign policy relationship remains stable and on a positive footing," Putin said.Xi echoed the Russian leader's remarks, calling on both countries to take the lead in advancing multipolarisation and democratisation in international relations amid global uncertainty."We must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers lead and advance the multipolarisation of the world and the democratisation of international relations," Xi said.He also called for deeper cooperation across various sectors, saying the partnership had contributed to stability in an increasingly turbulent international environment."Our relationship has brought greater stability and certainity to a turbulent world."Xi further described Russia-China relations as a model of equality, mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the Asia- Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Article Title: Peace through strength: Quad confronts economic coercion, unilateral actions
Article Text:
PM Modi pitched a Quad meeting in early 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Amid doubts not about Quad's survival but the level at which it will function, the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the US - PM Anthony Albanese, PM Narendra Modi, PM Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump respectively - met in Manila Tuesday for the first summit in 2 years.They looked to turn up the heat on China as they expressed grave concerns over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and committed to working together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.The president described Quad as very important and special - and Modi as a friend and a great leader - in his opening remarks, as he announced Quad will conduct its first exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft, working to protect "peace through strength".However, the short joint press release – unlike the expansive 2024 Wilmington Declaration – cut Beijing some slack by not explicitly mentioning South or East China Sea even though it strongly opposed any "destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability".Modi pitched hosting a Quad business leaders’ summit early next year.The meeting took place hours before Trump's departure for China, where he is set to attend a potentially landmark trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. Trump said Quad nations had reached several new critical mineral deals to secure their supply chains and ensure that none of them remained vulnerable to coercion by any single foreign supplier.The joint statement that P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context "making our seas safer". The exercise will take place in Guam next year under the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative that was launched in May this year to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.Importantly for India – amid growing US-Pakistan ties – the joint statement unequivocally condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and committed to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism.Calling the meeting in Manila an important milestone, Modi said that for India, Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership. "From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific," he said in his opening remarks, underlining the political will behind the partnership.The statement also said that Quad is working to secure critical supply chains, protecting freedom of navigation and overflight, driving growth through technologies of the future including investments and deployment of trusted Artificial Intelligence (AI), and responding to disasters with life-saving assistance.Expectedly, AI was a major area of focus with the leaders backing AI Accelerator, which was announced by the foreign ministers on the margins of the G20 meeting in Atlanta, and is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific. "We want to ensure that the future of this critical technology is dominated by nations that share our values and our common interests," said Trump.Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said that the Quad leaders agreed to launch a Quad business forum for the first time bringing together businesses, academics and industries to foster greater business ties across private sectors, including the promotion of commercial deals and partnerships critical to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.The joint statement recalled that this year marks nearly a decade since the Quad was revived and the tenth anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese PM Shinzo Abe in 2016. "A decade on, that vision is stronger than ever. Together, we have shown that the Quad is a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability, and prosperity," it said.
Article Summary: The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the US - PM Anthony Albanese, PM Narendra Modi, PM Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump respectively - met in Manila Tuesday for the first summit in 2 years. They expressed grave concerns over economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions, and committed to working together to ensure open, safe, and resilient maritime transit corridors.

Article Title: After govt push, curbs on sexual post recommendations on Instagram
Article Text:
Meta, which owns Instagram, said the platform now recommends fewer sexually suggestive posts and depictions of violence. (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Meta has tightened Instagram 's recommendations in India, disclosing the changes a month after the govt asked it to review how Instagram and Facebook suggest posts. Meta said Instagram now recommends fewer sexually suggestive posts and depictions of violence.The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. Posts complying with Instagram's rules can remain on the platform even if they are excluded from recommendations.Meta said it had strengthened its default safeguards over the past year based on user feedback. Instagram uses AI models to assess posts before recommending them and has fine-tuned its systems for India to identify more sensitive material."We've seen people report recommended content about half as often as they were a year ago," Meta said in a blog post. The company did not disclose the underlying figures.In its Oct 10 advisory, the IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material. It also sought stronger checks on posts that could incite violence or disrupt public order.The IT ministry asked Meta to ensure that users were not disproportionately exposed to a narrow set of narratives and to report back on the steps it had taken. Meta did not link the Instagram changes to the advisory or say whether it had changed how either platform recommends posts about events in India.
Article Summary: The changes apply to suggested posts from accounts users do not follow, including in Reels, and the main feed. The IT ministry asked Meta to review how it ranks and recommends posts, citing concerns that its systems could give undue prominence to misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material.

Article Title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan's conviction; offers son, wife relief

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate and granted the same relief to Khan's son and wife, who were denied this benefit by the high court.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned the HC for discriminating among them. It said there was "apparent legal dichotomy in the judgement". It said, "We find that the HC failed to articulate any coherent legal reason why similar relief, as granted to Mohammad Azam Khan, was denied, even though all three were convicted under the self-same charge of conspiracy."Where several convicts standing on the same footing seek stay/suspension of conviction, it is legitimate for them to expect similar treatment... Parity being a facet of Article 14 of Constitution, equals ought to be treated equally unless, of course, an intelligible differentia having a rational nexus with the object of the order distinguishes one from the others," the bench said.SC said though differential treatment was not forbidden, "an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained". It said, "If the court grants a stay/suspension of conviction to one... while similar relief to other similarly situated convicts is denied, the distinguishing feature on the record must be identified and expressly stated as the reason for the departure from parity. An order silent on that point is, by itself, arbitrary. "
Article Summary: Supreme Court Tuesday upheld Allahabad HC's order staying the conviction of SP neta Azam Khan in a case relating to the forgery of a birth certificate. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said all three were on the same footing and questioned HC for discriminating among them.

Article Title: Indian inventor patents new technique to transmute elements, reports gold in tests
Article Text:
Bengaluru inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements, with lab tests reporting gold and silver in processed samples

How it works

.

Larger ambition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: What if one chemical element could be converted into several others, including gold? An Indian inventor from Bengaluru has received a patent for a process that could do this using specially generated frequencies, without conventional nuclear reactors or radioactive reactions.There is no fission or fusion reaction here. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples.Rajah Vijay Kumar’s invention, called Gravitoradiophysical Nuclear Transmutation (GNT), has been granted Indian patent (No. 5683222), nearly eight years after it was filed on Nov 21, 2017. The patent was granted in the second half of 2025.“The GNT could eventually find applications in energy, medicine, genetics, industry and space,” Kumar, director and chief scientific officer, Scalene Energy Research Institute, Organization de Scalene Foundation, told TOI.To understand the process, it helps to know what makes one element different from another. Every element has atoms, and at the centre of each atom is a nucleus. The number of protons in this nucleus determines the element’s identity.Gold, for example, has 79 protons, while mercury has 80. Turning mercury into gold would therefore require changing the structure of its nucleus by removing (or displacing) one proton and one electron, something an ordinary chemical reaction cannot do.Kumar’s proposed process uses a specially designed reactor to achieve this. Its central component, called the ‘Boom Tube’, a tubular reactor that produces continuous free fall and weightlessness at molecular levels, fitted with antennas made from an aluminium alloy and connected to a high power high frequency generator. The apparatus also has systems to regulate temperature and pressure in a vacuum environment.The process works in two proposed stages. First, one frequency is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. A second frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus.The process works in two proposed stages. First, a disassociating frequency depending on the interested elements is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. Then, an element specific transmutation frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus. The exact mechanism of action is still being studied.As Kumar explains: “Every element has a unique frequency, or set of frequencies, that can break its chemical bonds and separate it from a compound. For the initial experiments, I chose mercury, which it describes as one of the heavier elements that could be handled relatively safely in its experimental setup. The aim, however, was not simply to make gold.”The larger ambition was to develop a process that can convert different elements and isotopes for possible applications in energy, medicine, industry and space exploration.The patent describes experiments in which a mercury compound, mercuric sulphate, was mixed with distilled water and processed through the reactor. An untreated portion was retained for comparison. An accredited laboratory, reportedly unaware of which samples had been processed, analysed both.The results reported gold at 1.91 mg per litre in the first processed sample and 2.3 milligrams per litre in the second. Silver was also detected at 11 milligrams per litre in the second test. Other elements, including magnesium, manganese, phosphorus and zinc, were reported in the processed samples. The mercury came down from 33.45 gm to 8.67 gm while sulphur almost remained unchanged at around 8.5 gm.The laboratory used a technique called Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which identifies and measures the quantities of elements in a sample. The research team acknowledges that considerable work under different conditions remains before the process can be perfected or considered for large-scale applications.There is also an important scientific caveat. Detecting gold, silver or other elements in a sample does not, by itself, mean the technology or process is ready for wider use immediately. The laboratory technique measures what is present, not how it was formed. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly the science of how such claimed transmutation has occurred.
Article Summary: Inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly how such claimed transmutation has occurred.

BENGALURU: A doctoral researcher at the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) has been selected for the 2026 Google PhD Fellowship, becoming the first PhD student from the institute to receive the recognition.Surya Sarathi Das, who works in the laboratory of Sabarinathan Radhakrishnan at NCBS, has been selected in the Health Research category, representing India. The fellowship, supported by Google.org, will fund his research exploring how artificial intelligence (AI) can help assess the risk of cervical cancer recurrence using routinely available digital pathology data.Das’ doctoral research examines how the integration of human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA into the tumour genome and the expression of viral genes influence tumour behaviour and patient outcomes. A key focus is understanding why some patients experience a recurrence of cervical cancer while others do not.His team has identified a molecular marker that could help distinguish patients at higher risk of relapse. With the fellowship support, Das plans to develop and evaluate AI models that can predict this biomarker directly from digital pathological data. This could potentially make risk assessment more affordable and accessible, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare settings.“Through my PhD research, I have been trying to understand why some patients with cervical cancer experience recurrence while others do not. With the support from Google, I hope to take this work further by exploring AI-based approaches to predict this marker and assess recurrence risks,” Das said.Radhakrishnan said the research could help clinicians improve patient stratification and tailor treatment and follow-up based on individual risks, with the long-term objective of reducing recurrence.Das is among 148 researchers selected for the 2026 fellowship across 38 countries. Google.org is providing $13 million in funding for this year's cohort. The programme supports early-career researchers advancing the science of AI, offering financial assistance for doctoral research and opportunities to engage with a global network of researchers.Since its launch in 2009, the Google PhD Fellowship Programme has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended slogans such as “Batenge toh katenge” and “Ek hain toh safe hain”, saying they were intended to remind people of the state's past law-and-order problems and encourage vigilance rather than polarise voters.Speaking at the News18 Rising Bharat Summit: North Edition, Adityanath said the younger generation needed to understand the conditions in Uttar Pradesh a decade ago to appreciate the changes made since then.“The question is not of polarisation; it is of being alert and cautious,” he said, according to news agency ANI.The chief minister said young people, particularly those aged between 15 and 25-27, should learn about the circumstances their parents had experienced. He alleged that Uttar Pradesh had faced an identity crisis, riots, lawlessness, insecurity among women and extortion during the previous Samajwadi Party (SP) government.“Today's youth, particularly those aged between 15 and 25-27 years, need to know what Uttar Pradesh was like 10 years ago. They need to understand the circumstances their parents went through,” he said.Explaining the slogan “Batenge toh katenge”, Adityanath referred to incidents during the SP government's tenure, including the Jawahar Bagh violence in Mathura, the Muzaffarnagar riots and communal clashes in Kosi Kalan, Aligarh and Bareilly.He alleged that riots were frequent under the SP government, while claiming that Uttar Pradesh was now “riot-free and curfew-free” under the BJP administration.Referring to the 2016 Jawahar Bagh violence, the chief minister alleged that a person associated with the SP had occupied hundreds of acres of land in the park.Two police personnel, then Superintendent of Police Mukul Dwivedi and Station House Officer Santosh Yadav, were killed during the operation to clear the encroachment. The CJI asked the petitioner’s counsel to make detailed submissions when the matter comes up before the appropriate bench on Friday.Advocate Rizwan Ahmed sought urgent intervention, alleging that Filibeck, the Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had interfered in India’s domestic political affairs by criticising the government and expressing support for the Opposition at the summit.Seeking an early hearing, Ahmed told the bench that the event had been organised in Telangana under the aegis of the state government and certain foundations, including the Samruddha Bharat Foundation. NEW DELHI: Travellers arriving in India from countries like Nigeria, Kenya, and Venezuela affected by yellow fever without a valid vaccination certificate could face quarantine for up to six days, with the cost to be borne by them, while airlines will have to pay for their transportation to designated facilities. This is among the key changes proposed in the draft Indian Aircraft (Public Health) Rules, 2026, which seek to replace the 1954 regulations.Under the existing rules, unvaccinated travellers could be isolated for up to nine days from the last possible exposure. The new draft proposes a maximum six-day quarantine counted from the date of departure from the yellow fever-affected country. Travellers unwilling to undergo quarantine can be denied entry and sent back without leaving the airport transit area.The proposed rules also seek to widen airport health oversight beyond specific infectious diseases to cover pandemics, public-health emergencies and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive hazards.Airport food outlets and flight kitchens will have to be licensed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Drinking water quality will have to be tested at source, with regular reports submitted to Airport Health Officers, who can order unsafe food to be discarded and close establishments or water sources found unsafe.The 1954 rules required aircraft disinsection in specific situations, including flights arriving from areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases or yellow fever. The 2026 draft proposes making disinsection mandatory for all arriving aircraft, while also requiring airport premises and surrounding areas extending at least 400 metres beyond the airport perimeter to be kept free of mosquitoes, rats and other disease-carrying vectors.Airlines will face more detailed reporting obligations, including submission of passenger manifests and information on illness or deaths on board. Airport Health Officers can seek passenger locator forms, contact details, destinations, travel itineraries and seat numbers, even outside a public-health emergency.The draft also introduces a defined penalty schedule and a two-stage appeal mechanism against orders passed by Airport Health Officers. It specifies monetary penalties for different violations, while appeals can be filed within 30 days and should, as far as possible, be disposed of within 60 days.The health ministry has invited comments from government departments, airport operators, airlines and other stakeholders within 30 days of its November 16 memorandum. The draft will be forwarded to the Ministry of Civil Aviation for further action after the suggestions are examined.
Article Summary: India has unveiled draft regulations enhancing quarantine protocols for travelers from yellow fever-affected nations. Unvaccinated travellers could be isolated for up to nine days from the last possible exposure. Travellers unwilling to undergo quarantine can be denied entry and sent back without leaving the airport transit area.

Article Title: NMC asks medical colleges to vet draft rules seeking tighter checks on animal experiments
Article Text:
The National Medical Commission has introduced new draft rules to enhance the ethical treatment of laboratory animals in research.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The use of laboratory animals in medical research could face tighter restrictions, with draft rules requiring researchers to explore alternatives to live animals wherever scientifically possible, minimise their numbers and reduce pain and suffering. The proposals also seek to prohibit experiments involving severe suffering that is likely to be prolonged and cannot be alleviated.In a public notice issued on Monday, the National Medical Commission (NMC) asked Deans, Principals and Heads of medical colleges and institutions to submit their comments, objections and suggestions to the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) within 30 days. The draft rules were notified on September 30 and published in the Gazette of India on October 6.The rules place the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement at the centre of animal research. They classify experiments as non-recovery, mild, moderate and severe, and prohibit those likely to cause prolonged, severe suffering that cannot be alleviated.Veterinary supervision would be mandatory for all experiments, with every establishment involved in animal research or breeding required to appoint a veterinarian.Each establishment would also have to set up a nine-member Institutional Animal Ethics Committee, with a three-year tenure, to oversee experiments. The committee would include scientists, a biologist, a veterinarian and four CCSEA nominees, and meet at least twice a year.The draft also seeks to avoid death as an experimental endpoint wherever possible, requiring researchers to use early humane endpoints. Where death is unavoidable, the number of animals affected and the duration and intensity of suffering must be minimised. Establishments would have to maintain records of euthanasia, including the method, dosage and reason.The use of stray and feral domestic animals would be restricted, with exceptions allowed only when their use is scientifically justified. Experiments on non-human primates would be permitted only for narrowly defined research purposes where no other species can serve the objective.All establishments conducting animal experiments or breeding, housing and trading laboratory animals would require CCSEA registration and face inspections at least twice a year. Violations could invite a 15-day notice to rectify deficiencies, followed by suspension or cancellation for repeated non-compliance. Immediate action would be allowed in cases of imminent risk to animal welfare.
Article Summary: The National Medical Commission has introduced new draft rules to enhance the ethical treatment of laboratory animals in research. The rules place the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement at the centre of animal research. Experiments on non-human primates would be permitted only for narrowly defined research purposes where no other species can serve the objective.
